scope: N699 read-only implementation and acceptance audit. Exact eb72 source. No code/test/canonical edits, packages, worktrees, profiles, tests, GPU, credentials, ~/.ssh reads or SSH/network connections. Public official documentation browsing only. First CI failure preempts held work.

``timeout`` is floored at one second before the call, so the sentence

existing_cases.docstring: The ``profile add`` arguments map one-for-one onto the stored record.

existing_cases.name: test_an_unknown_profile_subcommand_is_rejected_by_the_handler
existing_cases.docstring:
``_cmd_profile`` refuses a namespace it does not recognise.

The parser makes the subcommand mandatory, so this reaches the handler
only by calling it directly -- which is what a future subcommand added to
the parser but not the handler would do.

existing_cases.docstring: A ``SettingsError`` becomes a remote-execution error, not a traceback.

existing_cases.docstring: ``--set`` values are validated locally so a cluster job never starts wrong.

existing_cases.name: test_submit_runs_the_profile_command_and_records_the_job
existing_cases.docstring: A full submission through the ``command`` backend persists a queued job.

existing_cases.name: test_submitting_to_a_profile_that_does_not_exist_is_a_usage_error
existing_cases.docstring: The profile is resolved before the job record is created.

existing_cases.docstring: No jobs prints the header and an explicit empty note.

existing_cases.docstring: One job renders as one compact row naming its remote ID.

existing_cases.name: test_a_job_with_no_remote_id_renders_a_dash
existing_cases.docstring: ``_job_row`` shows an em dash where a remote ID has not arrived yet.

existing_cases.name: test_a_job_error_is_appended_to_its_row
existing_cases.docstring: A row that carries an error shows it after the remote ID.

existing_cases.docstring: ``--refresh`` runs each active job's status command before printing.

existing_cases.name: test_status_prints_the_row_and_the_log_tail
existing_cases.docstring: ``status --logs`` shows the compact row followed by the retrieved tail.

existing_cases.docstring: ``status --json`` emits the whole job record and no table.

existing_cases.docstring: ``status`` is the exit code of the remote job, so scripts can branch on it.

existing_cases.docstring: An unrecognised job ID is a sentence on stderr, not a traceback.

existing_cases.name: test_cancel_prints_the_new_state
existing_cases.docstring: Cancelling runs the profile's cancel command and persists ``cancelled``.

existing_cases.name: test_logs_prints_the_retrieved_tail
existing_cases.docstring: ``logs`` prints exactly what the profile's log command produced.

existing_cases.name: test_logs_without_a_log_command_explains_how_to_add_one
existing_cases.docstring: A command profile with no log command says what is missing.

existing_cases.name: test_watch_polls_until_the_job_is_terminal
existing_cases.docstring: ``watch`` keeps polling while the job runs and stops when it succeeds.

existing_cases.name: test_watch_returns_nonzero_for_a_job_that_failed
existing_cases.docstring: A watched job that ends in failure exits nonzero on the first poll.

existing_cases.name: test_watch_can_print_the_log_tail_when_it_finishes
existing_cases.docstring: ``watch --logs`` retrieves the tail once the job reaches a terminal state.

existing_cases.name: test_an_interrupt_is_reported_rather_than_a_traceback
existing_cases.docstring: Ctrl-C during a long poll exits with the runtime code and one word.

existing_cases.name: test_a_missing_command_is_an_argparse_usage_error
existing_cases.docstring: The subcommand is mandatory: no command exits 2 through argparse.

existing_cases.name: test_the_parser_names_every_shipped_subcommand
existing_cases.docstring: ``build_parser`` exposes the documented command set.

existing_cases.name: test_the_module_entry_point_exits_zero_on_a_command_that_worked
existing_cases.docstring:
A successful listing leaves the process with status 0.

Returning the handler's value without raising would leave the exit code
at 0 for failures too, which is the one thing a scheduler watches.

existing_cases.name: test_the_module_entry_point_exits_nonzero_when_the_job_is_unknown
existing_cases.docstring: A usage failure reaches the shell as a non-zero status, with a reason.

existing_cases.name: test_every_profile_setting_has_label_help_and_remote_api_link
existing_cases.docstring:
The link is in the label's help; nothing is drawn beside the label.

A teal dot used to carry it. The dot is what was pointed at the module
page while the label's own help -- built with its arguments the other
way round -- named the help text as the module and landed on the
documentation index. With the dot gone, the help is the only route, so
it is the help that is measured.

existing_cases.name: test_hovering_a_profile_label_shows_its_help_and_its_link
existing_cases.docstring:
Measured through the popup the reader gets, not the property alone.

A native Qt tooltip cannot be walked into, so a link inside one cannot
be clicked. The sticky popup can, which is why the labels claim it.

existing_cases.name: test_a_language_change_repoints_every_profile_label
existing_cases.docstring:
The API pages are per language, and the labels' links have to follow.

The dot answered to ``set_url`` from the language pass. The label
answers to ``refresh_api_tooltips``, which is the same pass reaching
setting help — and which never reached these labels while their
module key and setting key were the wrong way round.

existing_cases.name: test_a_backend_the_dialog_does_not_offer_falls_back_to_the_first
existing_cases.docstring: A profile written by a newer build still opens rather than crashing.

existing_cases.name: test_renaming_a_profile_writes_the_new_one_before_dropping_the_old
existing_cases.docstring: A disk error must not erase the only usable profile.

existing_cases.name: test_a_threaded_operation_runs_off_the_gui_thread
existing_cases.docstring: Every network call goes through ``make_thread``; this is that path.

existing_cases.name: test_closing_the_screen_takes_its_remote_calls_with_it
existing_cases.docstring: An ownerless REST call keeps the application from being able to quit.

existing_cases.name: test_a_worker_that_will_not_answer_is_still_released
existing_cases.docstring: Cancellation and interruption are attempts, not preconditions.

existing_cases.name: test_the_editor_still_saves_when_its_buttons_cannot_be_styled
existing_cases.docstring:
Styling is decoration; Save and Cancel have to work regardless.

The dialog looks its standard buttons up by role so it can mark Save
primary and Cancel destructive. If a style or platform ever hands back
nothing for that lookup, the guarded styling must be the only thing lost:
were the ``accepted``/``rejected`` wiring to sit behind the same guard,
the profile editor would open with two buttons that do nothing and no way
to save a profile at all -- an unusable screen, not an unstyled one.

existing_cases.name: test_a_cancelled_new_profile_writes_nothing_to_disk
existing_cases.docstring:
Cancel must mean cancel, or half-typed profiles pile up in the combo.

The editor is filled in before the user decides. If the screen read the
dialog's fields without first checking that it was accepted, pressing
Cancel would still save the half-typed profile, and the profile combo --
which is what Submit sends a job through -- would fill with entries the
user explicitly refused.

existing_cases.name: test_a_cancelled_edit_leaves_the_stored_profile_untouched
existing_cases.docstring:
A cancelled edit that still writes is silent data loss.

Editing loads the stored profile into the dialog, so every field is
already populated with something plausible. If Cancel were treated like
Save, the poll interval, host, and command lines the user was midway
through changing would be persisted over a working profile and the next
submission would go somewhere else.

existing_cases.name: test_saving_a_profile_under_its_own_name_does_not_delete_it
existing_cases.docstring:
The rename cleanup must fire on a rename and only on a rename.

An edit is stored as "save the new record, then drop the old name". When
the name did not change, those are the same record: running the cleanup
anyway would delete the profile the user just saved and leave the screen
with no profile to submit through. This drives both halves -- a real
rename, which must drop the old name, and an ordinary edit, which must
not.

existing_cases.name: test_a_finished_worker_with_no_callback_still_frees_the_screen
existing_cases.docstring:
The screen must unlock even when the result has no home to go to.

``_pending_callback`` is cleared or never set for a worker whose caller
has gone away. Calling ``None`` there would raise straight out of a Qt
slot, and the exception would leave the screen believing an operation is
still running: Submit, Refresh, Cancel and Logs all stay disabled and the
user has to reopen the module to get them back.

existing_cases.name: test_only_the_commands_a_profile_actually_configures_are_redacted
existing_cases.docstring:
The record is meant to be pasted into a bug report unedited.

Custom command lines can carry hosts, paths and account names, so every
configured one is replaced. A profile that configures none -- an ssh or
slurm profile, where those fields are empty -- must not come back with
four ``<configured command>`` placeholders instead: that would tell a
maintainer reading the report that commands were set when they were not,
and send them looking for the wrong bug.

existing_cases.name: test_a_pair_whose_worker_is_already_gone_is_still_drained
existing_cases.docstring:
A half-reaped pair must not stop the screen draining its threads.

``_workers`` holds ``(thread, worker)`` pairs and the worker half can
already be gone by the time the module is closed. Cancelling is attempted
per pair, but the thread must be interrupted and drained either way: a
thread that is never drained stays in the process-wide run registry, and
that registry is what ``MainWindow.closeEvent`` consults when it decides
whether spaCR is allowed to quit. One missed pair and the application
refuses to close.

existing_cases.name: test_the_button_waits_for_a_snapshot
existing_cases.docstring: Disabled until Submit remote… sends one, and again once edited.

existing_cases.name: test_saving_writes_the_snapshot_and_keeps_submit_unchanged
existing_cases.docstring: The CSV holds the snapshot; the snapshot is still what Submit sends.

existing_cases.name: test_cancel_and_write_failures
existing_cases.docstring: Cancel leaves the status; a failed write is said in the status.

actual_entry_points.behavior: Existing button is Submit remote…, not a dedicated cluster popup. It collects settings and emits a snapshot through remote_submit_requested; no authentication UI.
MainWindow navigates to Distributed Jobs and seeds configure_submission.

ExecutionProfileDialog creates/edits profiles; manual host alias or user@host, backend, workdir, path map, runner and scheduler options. No separate user/port/key/jump fields, SSH chooser or Test connection.

ExecutionProfile stores host only for connection. Dataclass validation blocks host options/newlines and preserves shell-free command templates. ProfileStore and RemoteJob snapshots persist plain JSON.

Every remote operation creates an external ssh command with the alias and quoted remote command. OpenSSH may honor existing user/system Includes, host patterns, ProxyJump/ProxyCommand and ControlMaster, but spaCR does not discover or control them.

subprocess.run captures output and optionally pipes input. No terminal, prompt broker, SSH_ASKPASS setup or persistent library connection. stdin carries settings payload during upload, so it cannot be repurposed as a password channel.
Upload is a quoted remote mkdir/cat command with umask077, not a recursive dataset copy. It can authenticate separately from submit, polling, cancellation and log retrieval.
Network manager operations run in a make_thread worker, with one busy operation and Qt timer polling. No worker-to-GUI challenge/response seam or connection reuse pool.

dependency_state.transport: System OpenSSH executable on PATH. No paramiko or asyncssh declaration/import in these source paths or setup/pyproject.
dependency_state.consequence: Selecting a persistent library transport requires an explicit dependency/bundling decision and native package verification, rather than assuming it is already available. Existing OpenSSH config compatibility is a useful starting point.

spec_gap_matrix.requirement: Find my SSH settings and manual chooser
spec_gap_matrix.current: Absent. A manual OpenSSH target field exists.
spec_gap_matrix.future_acceptance: Synthetic discovery roots on Unix/macOS and Windows, unreadable/missing files, alias list and manual folder choice. Never read private key contents or modify SSH files; store paths and configuration provenance only.

spec_gap_matrix.current: Delegated implicitly to external OpenSSH only; no parser or displayed effective config.
spec_gap_matrix.future_acceptance: Host matching/negation/default precedence, nested conditional Includes, lexical globs, cycles and bounded expansion, multiple IdentityFiles, quoted paths, tokens and explicit GUI overrides. Preserve original alias so filling HostName does not bypass its matching config.

spec_gap_matrix.current: No Windows config discovery; system ssh may use its own defaults.
spec_gap_matrix.future_acceptance: USERPROFILE/.ssh/config, PROGRAMDATA OpenSSH system config when applicable, spaces, drive paths, separator/case handling and selected folder. No credential file scans outside declared search roots.

Plain hostnames and bracketed non-default ports; safely skip hashed entries and certificate/revocation markers. known_hosts is a host-key database, not a source of username, port defaults, private key paths or authentication secrets.

spec_gap_matrix.current: Absent; captured subprocess has no Qt interaction. Existing agent/terminal/config authentication may work externally but is not an in-app MFA feature.
spec_gap_matrix.future_acceptance: Fake two-step server challenges, instructions and echo flags, empty prompt/push wait, approve/deny/timeout/cancel/retry, repeated challenges and late worker completion. Prompt wording is server-authored plain text, not locally translated; passwords/OTP responses never logged, journaled or saved.

spec_gap_matrix.current: OpenSSH alias may already specify ProxyJump or ProxyCommand. No chooser/editor field.
spec_gap_matrix.future_acceptance: One/multiple hops, per-hop user and port, password/MFA/key combinations, failed jump attribution. Each server may demand its own authentication; do not promise one approval total across separate hops.

spec_gap_matrix.current: Each operation starts ssh. User-supplied ControlMaster may reuse a connection, but no app-owned lifecycle or cross-platform guarantee.
spec_gap_matrix.future_acceptance: One authenticated session per effective destination/profile/user/auth context shared by Test/upload/submit/poll/log/cancel. Verify backend capability on each OS; reconnect after expiry/network loss with one coordinated prompt, not repeated polling dialogs. Close only app-owned transports/control sockets, never another session master.

GUI states for local client/config, connection/host key, authentication, hostname, Slurm sinfo and executable/workdir/path prerequisites. Slurm check applies to Slurm targets; workstation profiles should not falsely fail because sinfo is absent.

important_design_findings.finding: Using ssh -G blindly is not a passive read-only parser. It evaluates Host and Match, and Match exec can run a local command. No such command was executed by this audit.
important_design_findings.plan: Use a bounded static discovery parser without executing directives. If choosing authoritative OpenSSH effective resolution later, disclose and handle Match exec semantics instead of advertising it as purely passive.

important_design_findings.finding: SSH authentication input must be separate from payload stdin and worker output. Settings upload currently pipes JSON into the command.
important_design_findings.plan: Add a typed authentication broker at the existing runner seam. Evaluate OpenSSH askpass/multiplex versus an optional persistent library transport using controlled tests before choosing; do not replace capture-only command execution with an unbounded PTY transcript parser.

important_design_findings.finding: Authentication timeout and command timeout need separate treatment. A 30s squeue operation cannot silently consume repeated MFA prompts; errors must name the exact failing stage.
important_design_findings.plan: Bound authentication and challenge retries independently, pause automatic polling while auth is pending, propagate cancellation/close and prevent late callbacks from touching destroyed dialogs.

important_design_findings.finding: Unknown/changed host keys need a separate verified trust decision; never disable host-key checking to make MFA tests pass.
important_design_findings.plan: Use existing host-key policy. Show fingerprint and target for a new trust choice, reject mismatch by default; do not write user known_hosts without explicit supported permission.

official_Great_Lakes_findings.policies: Current official policy describes UM Kerberos password plus Okta for interactive sessions; the source feature’s Duo statement is historical, so implementation and help must remain vendor-neutral.
official_Great_Lakes_findings.key_auth: Official FAQ says SSH public/private key authentication is not currently supported for Great Lakes. Key discovery is still useful for other hosts, but cannot replace Great Lakes MFA.
official_Great_Lakes_findings.not_verified: No current maintainer hostname, account permissions, VPN/network path, live prompt sequence, scheduler account/partition or server multiplex/session policy was accessed.

user_strings_and_alpha.current: ExecutionProfileDialog has translated title, intro and backend labels, but several literal placeholders/tooltips and Submit remote… already bypass direct tr. Do not treat existing strings as authorization for new untracked prose.
new_contracts: SSH configuration/alias picker and effective field labels
Server, username, port, identity path, jump host, config source and session options help
Test connection, authentication pending, approve on your device, cancelled/denied/timed-out/retry, hostname and Slurm results
Great Lakes example with Kerberos and server-driven MFA rather than a hard-coded vendor
user_strings_and_alpha.rules: All authored strings through tr(), exact source-bound runtime/compact ownership, all nine locale repairs by normal tools. Server prompts stay literal server text with echo policy; do not persist responses. No new spacr modules or authored # comments.
user_strings_and_alpha.alpha: N699 is in features/new, not features/future, so the future-item alpha rule does not automatically gate it. Existing Distributed Jobs is already shipped. Preserve the existing alpha Allocated GPUs checkbox registered under item493; any new alpha-only controls need ALPHA_FEATURES plus literal setObjectName. No change was made.

integration_batches.acceptance: Concrete displayed connection information from synthetic fixtures; no network/MFA claim.

integration_batches.scope: Authentication broker and one persistent transport/session at existing runner seam, jump host support and Qt challenges.
integration_batches.tests: Controlled fake SSH server or fake transport with genuine challenge semantics; two-stage approval, denial, timeouts, cancel, host-key mismatch, prompts on GUI thread, response secrecy, one auth reused across operations and reconnect. No personal SSH configuration or real cluster.

integration_batches.scope: Test connection staged results and integration with upload/Slurm/status/logs/cancel plus application close.
integration_batches.tests: Existing backend semantics, commands/quoting/settings-file integrity, scheduler accounting fallback, transient network errors, profile edits and no poll prompt storms; fake-stage hostname/sinfo results and exact failure attribution.

integration_batches.scope: Normal API/runtime/guide/help/consumer artifacts and nine locale translations, supported installer packaging.
integration_batches.tests: Generated source freshness, API/dataclass signature changes registered accurately, runtime i18n/alpha checks, Windows OpenSSH capability or selected optional transport packaged. No hand merge or ratchet ceiling change.

integration_batches.scope: Maintainer-operated Great Lakes acceptance after scoped implementation tests and CI.
integration_batches.requires: Actual authorized account, local network/VPN, current prompt method, host-key fingerprint and Slurm account/partition/workdir/installed spaCR environment. No passwords or OTPs sent to agents.
integration_batches.proof: One GUI login and its server challenges, successful hostname/sinfo, one tiny authorized sbatch job, squeue/sacct updates/logs/cancel over the same authenticated session without additional approval, plus denial/timeout/reconnect behavior. Record only redacted receipts.

maintainer_blockers: Confirm access and authorize one bounded real acceptance session after implementation; agent does not possess Great Lakes credentials or permission to connect now.
Provide non-secret host alias, expected network/VPN path and authorized Slurm account/partition/workdir plus compatible remote spaCR runner.
Complete MFA locally and confirm host-key trust using the official fingerprint/channel; never supply passwords or codes in chat.
Confirm real server policy allows connection sharing and whether jump hosts add independent MFA. Portable tests cannot certify university policy.
regeneration_contract: ExecutionProfile fields/documented public signatures and manager behavior may change; use normal API source/history generation and source-bound translations. Rebuild runtime catalogs/help/consumer/settings-flow artifacts only from final integrated source. All held N699 changes require their own exact-source CI after the current release; old eb72 CI does not certify them.
